subject: EU/APAC private-deploy: evacuation routing & residency assurance (follow-up)
messages:
From: Yuko Sato <yuko.sato@kaito.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: ACME Cloud Ops <acme-cloudops@example.com>
Date: Tue, 23 May 2028 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Private deploy residency question: APAC warm standby activation and EU data residency

Marcus — thanks for the call earlier. We reviewed the proposed warm-standby activation for our APAC site and have one thing we need to be explicit about for compliance: when the APAC standby becomes the active serving region for a portion of traffic, what guarantees can Redwood provide that EU-resident customer data remains within EU jurisdiction?

Specifically, we need:
- A short description of the routing and egress change (what headers/peering change) during an evacuation or failover window;
- Evidence that control-plane metadata or logs containing tenant-identifying info will not be egressed outside EU;
- Any mitigations (KMS key scoping, IP allowlists, egress ACLs) we should expect;

I've attached the diagram we drew up (network-diagram-v3.pdf) and an extract of our audit checklist. Can you loop in the ops and security folks who will provide the artifact we can present to our compliance team?

Thanks,
Yuko
Lead Cloud Security, Kaito Logistics

Attachments: network-diagram-v3.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Yuko Sato <yuko.sato@kaito.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 23 May 2028 11:02:14 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deploy residency question: APAC warm standby activation and EU data residency

Yuko — appreciate the clear checklist. Looping Grace (ops) and Soojin (legal/compliance) to provide the artifacts and proposed controls. High level response for now:

- Routing & egress: Redwood’s private deployment supports per-tenant egress policies. During a warm-standby activation we do NOT automatically change data egress unless explicitly configured in the tenant’s residency policy. In your configuration we recommend an EU-anchored control-plane + EU-only egress ACLs; traffic can be proxied through APAC compute for low-latency inference while encrypted payloads and tenant metadata remain pinned to EU KMS and log sinks.

- Control-plane metadata: control-plane operations that include tenant identifiers are optional and can be configured to use EU-only logging endpoints or direct S3 endpoints in the customer VPC (we provide signed telemetry proxies).

- Mitigations: KMS key scoping (customer-managed keys), IP-level egress allowlists, and per-tenant KV cache scoping are the three main levers we propose. We can produce a short evidence bundle (network diagram with peering arrows, egress ACL export, and a sample KMS key binding log) for your compliance review.

Grace / Soojin — can you confirm availability to assemble the evidence bundle? Yuko — any timeline constraints for your audit committee?

Best,
Marcus
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Yuko Sato <yuko.sato@kaito.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 24 May 2028 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deploy residency question: APAC warm standby activation and EU data residency

Yuko — thanks for the checklist and Marcus for the summary. A couple of compliance notes and a proposed deliverable list below. We cannot assert legal jurisdiction beyond our contractual commitments, but operationally we can provide the following artifacts to demonstrate technical controls that support your EU residency requirements:

Deliverables (we will package as a single zip with signed manifests):
1) Network diagram (annotated) showing peering, NAT/IP ranges, and BGP/route propagation behavior during failover windows (PDF; we will mark egress points).
2) Export of egress ACL configuration for the tenant (text) and a sample netflow capture showing only EU egress IPs in the configured mode.
3) KMS binding log (kms-handshake-log.txt) showing key usage records scoped to the EU key ARN and audit log entries with timestamps and signer identity.
4) Control-plane telemetry policy document (short) explaining which telemetry fields are suppressed/hashed when EU-only mode is selected.

Operational constraints to call out now: if you require zero cross-border compute (no APAC execution whatsoever), we will need to pin both control-plane and serving compute to EU-only hosts which will increase failover RTO and may require a capacity reservation in EU. If you are okay with APAC execution but EU-bound egress and keying, the plan above is workable without capacity reservations.

Grace — can ops produce the netflow sample and the annotated diagram by Friday EOD PST? Marcus — I’ll coordinate on the signed manifests.

Regards,
Soojin Lee
Head of Legal & Compliance (contracts), Redwood Inference

From: ACME Cloud Ops <acme-cloudops@example.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Yuko Sato <yuko.sato@kaito.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 May 2028 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deploy residency question: APAC warm standby activation and EU data residency

Thanks all — this is perfect. Kaito’s compliance team wants the evidence bundle and a short tabletop runbook that lists the exact manual steps Redwood will take during an evacuation (who announces the switch, what firewall rules are applied, how long keys are rotated). Proposed timeline: artifact bundle by Mon 2028-05-28, tabletop session Thurs 2028-05-31 09:00 BST. Please confirm and we’ll issue a DocuSign PO for the evidence artifact review and tabletop facilitation.

ACME Ops (on behalf of Kaito)
